semantic_edges.summary: Reusable content editor load fetches one reusable block including deleted markers, redirects deleted content to trash, and supplies folders plus block definitions for editor UI.
All reusable content edit actions require authenticated user before updating, publishing, or moving folders.
Reusable block update parses submitted JSON content and rejects empty payloads or content whose type differs from current block_type.
Folder update action prevents moving a folder into itself or one of its descendants before persisting parent_id.
Reusable content editor derives publish status, draft-change status, primary action label, disabled state, and hints from reusable block publish helpers plus local dirty state.
Reusable content editor uses reusableBlockEditor helpers for editable snapshots, field updates, nested block add/remove/move operations, validation, and submitted content shape.
Reusable content editor renders nested blocks through BlockListEditor for fields whose definition accepts block arrays, while disabling reusable references inside reusable blocks.
After successful save or publish, reusable content editor updates client reusable block store and block folder store without full invalidation.
Enhanced reusable content form emits success and failure toast messages for draft saves, publishing, and validation blockers.
Trash page load and page restore action combine deleted pages, active pages, restorePageById, and fresh page state so restored pages rejoin the normal CMS tree.
Trash page load and reusable content restore action combine deleted reusable blocks, active reusable blocks, restoreReusableBlock, and fresh library state.
Trash restore actions require authenticated user before restoring pages or reusable content.
Trash page hydrates active pages into pagesStore in browser and updates it from restorePage action results.
Trash page hydrates active reusable blocks into reusableBlocksStore and refreshes it after reusable content restore.
Deleted pages must be restored under an active parent; UI defaults to original parent when still active and disables restore until a parent is selected.
Trash page enhanced forms show restore success and failure toasts for page and reusable content recovery.
Trash page test mocks SvelteKit enhance/applyAction and verifies successful page restore appears once in toast stack.
Page editor load fetches page including deleted markers, redirects deleted pages to trash, reads draft version content/meta, and supplies page tree plus reusable blocks.
Page update action validates title/urlName/root rules and checks draft path segment conflicts under selected parent before saving draft identity.
Page update rejects missing parent for non-root pages, self-parenting, unknown parent pages, and moves into descendant page trees.
Page update and publish actions validate parsed page content against known reusable block IDs before saving or publishing.
Page editor parses existing draft meta and submitted SEO fields into canonical PageSeoMeta shape for draft updates and publish responses.
Page update and publish actions require authenticated user before draft mutation or publishing.
Page editor derives publish badge, draft-change state, primary action state, disabled state, and hints from page status helpers plus local dirty snapshot.
Page editor uses pageContentEditor helpers for editable content, block add/remove/move, field updates, reusable block reference insertion, and validation.
Page editor registers reusable block insertion handler so sidebar-driven insertion can append reusable references into current page draft.
Page editor renders page blocks through BlockListEditor and passes reusable block list, drag state, insertion handlers, and validation errors.
Page editor builds live path preview from title, urlName, parent selection, and page tree, falling back to current path if preview cannot be built.
After successful page draft save or publish, page editor updates pagesStore with returned pages without full invalidation.
Enhanced page editor form emits toast feedback for validation blockers, draft saves, publish success, and server failures.
Sidebar action endpoint requires API authentication before handling create/delete folder, reusable block delete, or page delete intents.
Sidebar API creates/deletes block folders and soft-deletes reusable blocks, then returns refreshed page, folder, block, and reference state.
Sidebar API removes reusable block references from pages before soft-deleting reusable content and validates page deletability before soft-deleting pages.
Dev layout supplies nested static page data to DevSidebarFrame as a reference fixture for sidebar behavior.
Dev layout composes Sidebar.Provider, DevSidebarFrame, Sidebar.Inset, trigger, separator, theme toggle, breadcrumbs, and route children to exercise inset sidebar shell.
DevSidebarFrame demonstrates expanded and icon-collapsed sidebar layouts, including header, content groups, menu buttons, footer account menu, and tooltips.
DevSidebarPageItem recursively renders nested pages with depth-based padding, collapsible child groups, actions menu, active-open state, and leaf/folder icons.
Design-system dev page showcases production UI primitives including buttons, button groups, inputs, select, textarea, tabs, overlays, feedback, progress, avatars, icons, tokens, and skeletons.
Dev index routes engineers to design-system reference surface for inspecting primitives, tokens, icons, and feedback states.
README defines Blockkit as SvelteKit, TypeScript, Tailwind, Supabase CMS experiment with install, Supabase, env, database reset, dev, and verification commands.
README states SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must stay server-only and not be exposed in browser code.
Changes queue requires agents to read repo instructions and docs index, maintain feature/refactor/bug entries, and update docs/agents alongside implementation work.
Queued work that references a design must review unresolved points, risks, defaults, and open questions before implementation and ask user when they affect scope.
Design document defines reusable block instances as separate CMS records grouped by block folders, independent from page URL hierarchy and backed by code-defined block types.
Reusable block entries must use blockType values from code registry, keep content.type aligned with blockType, and rely on app-layer validation.
Reusable block design requires sidebar Blocks section with collapsible folders, leaf block items, block type badges, and local collapse state alongside unchanged page navigation.
Page parent-based URL design informs page path behavior where parent hierarchy and urlName/title determine draft/live paths while root remains slash.
Page publish workflow design informs draft versus published status behavior surfaced by page editor primary actions and publish-state badges.
